source.title: How more data can hurt: Instability and regularization in next-generation reservoir computing
source.authors: Yuan-Zhao Zhang; Edmilson Roque dos Santos; Hui-Xin Zhang; Sean P. Cornelius

page_placements.theme: Reconstruction conditioning can propagate to dynamical instability

record.tranche_reason: The study measures how training-data amount affects NGRC prediction performance and explicitly distinguishes its instability result from double descent, reporting that it did not observe a second descent in this setting.
record.gate_note: The study reports its own data-size sweeps of basin-prediction error, which bear on V3. Flow-surface fitting errors and condition numbers are not test-error measures for the listed versions and are omitted. Statements about double descent and optimally tuned regularization drawn from cited work are not extracted as results of this study.
record.test_reason: The study shows more training data hurting NGRC basin prediction, but the cause is autoregressive instability in an over-determined ridge regression (about 21 features, thousands of samples per trajectory). That is far from any interpolation threshold, so no version is tested. Model size, epochs and threshold location are never varied. The authors say they saw no second descent and link to double descent only in the Discussion.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors find data-induced instability in NGRC from ill-conditioned current/delayed-state features, not flow-map overfitting. Proportional regularization or carefully tuned training noise fixes it. They note a possible link to double descent but saw no second descent, and suggest model-size sweeps as future work.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses next-generation reservoir computing for dynamical-system forecasting and basin reconstruction, not the original deep-network model-size, epoch, or sample-size double-descent experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: Instability onset depends on regularization strength; proportional regularization prevents the large-data transition over a reported intermediate range. Noise-based stabilization is sensitive to noise strength: σ = 8×10⁻⁵ fails, while σ = 1×10⁻⁴ stabilizes, and larger values rapidly degrade accuracy.

fits_no_version.finding: In NGRC on the magnetic pendulum, more noise-free trajectories at fixed ridge λ trigger a sudden instability (e.g. p 0.18→1 from Ntraj 100→1000 at λ=0.01). Onset is delayed by larger λ. Scaling λ with Ntraj, or adding input noise around σ=10⁻⁴, removes it. No second descent was seen.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In autoregressive data-driven dynamical models with delay features, more training data at fixed regularization can cause stability loss and worse prediction, independent of the interpolation threshold.

record.problems: The principal evidence is for NGRC on the magnetic pendulum; the displayed data-size curves are figures and exact transition thresholds are not stated. Basin-prediction error is not a test of an interpolation-threshold peak. The paper mentions Lorenz-system results in supplementary Fig. S1, but the supplied text does not provide their details.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted for the 60-row limit. Flow-map fitting-error curves and condition-number measurements were left out because they are not test-error results for the listed versions; cited findings from other work were also excluded.

untested.parts: Training time not varied (closed-form ridge solution).
No interpolation threshold; the model is heavily over-determined, so sample-wise harm near the threshold is not examined.
No double-descent peak, label-noise or peak-splitting test; the regularization and input-noise results concern instability.

missing.what: Lorenz-system forecasting: larger regularization is needed for stability as Ntraj grows.
missing.locator: Section II B; Supplementary Fig. S1

missing.what: With k=1 (no delayed states), no instability occurs but prediction is poor.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's T5/tests classification and V3 links are rejected. V3 names a peak near the interpolation threshold, but this ridge regression has ~21 features against thousands of samples, and the harm comes from autoregressive instability. The double-descent material in the Discussion is cited from others' work.

versions.untested_parts: Training epochs or training time are not varied.
The study does not identify or measure an interpolation threshold; it varies the number of training trajectories in NGRC.
Capacity is not swept across an interpolation point to test a second descent.
The study does not test whether a single effective-complexity measure predicts peak locations across axes.

It does not test whether a double-descent peak is driven by label noise or variance, whether peaks split, or whether optimally tuned regularization removes such a peak. Its added noise is applied to training inputs, and its regularization results concern instability.
The study does not re-count complexity or test whether such a count turns a second descent into an ordinary U-shape.

relation.reason: Section III compares the findings with double descent and proposes a possible connection; model-size sweeps are future work.

tranche.reason: The results concern autonomous rollout instability in an overdetermined regression setting, without establishing V3's near-interpolation condition or testing another claim version. The authors report no second descent.

source_check.notes: The authors-conclusion paraphrase is accurate. Keep these results distinct from double-descent evidence; the supplied text is arXiv v3 dated 5 July 2025.

statements.correction: Table I: λ = 0.01; Ntraj = 100 gives p = 0.18; Ntraj = 1000 gives p = 1. p = wrong-attractor prediction rate. Fig. 9: suitable λNtraj regularization suppresses the instability transition. Fig. 11: fixed λ = 10⁻⁴; σ = 10⁻⁴ stabilizes across data sizes; σ = 8×10⁻⁵ does not.
statements.problem: p measures wrong-attractor predictions, not instability specifically. The noise remedy uses λ = 10⁻⁴; 'near 10⁻⁴' obscures the reported sensitivity, since σ = 8×10⁻⁵ fails.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: NGRC basin prediction on the magnetic pendulum and the reported training-input noise and regularization settings
reader_labels.reason: More trajectories can trigger worse prediction through instability, but the study does not locate an interpolation threshold; the effect is prevented by proportional regularization or by a narrow, suitable input-noise range (r1-r20).
